question: Which of the following bodies is authorised to change the name of any state of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The authority to change the name of a state in India is vested in the **Parliament of India**.
 
• This power is derived from **Article 3 of the Indian Constitution**, which allows the Parliament to change the name, area, or boundaries of a state.
 
• A **constitutional amendment is not required** for this process, making it relatively straightforward compared to other constitutional procedures.
 
• Before passing the bill for renaming a state, the **President of India refers the proposal** to the respective state legislature for its opinion; however, this opinion is **not binding**.
 
• The final decision is made when the bill is passed by a **simple majority** in both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Examples of State Name Changes:**

 
 
• **Madras** was renamed **Tamil Nadu** in 1969.
 
• **Bombay** was renamed **Maharashtra** in 1960.
 
• **Orissa** was renamed **Odisha** in 2011 through the Odisha (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2010.
